title: Value vs Reference Types in C#

scenes.say: Struct or class in C sharp? What's the real difference? Let's break it down.
Structs are value types, storing data directly. Classes are reference types, storing data on the heap. Records? They're reference types too, but focus on value-based equality.

scenes.code:
int x = 5;
object o = x; // Boxing
scenes.say: When you assign an integer to an object, that's called boxing. C sharp wraps the value type as a reference type.
Assign a struct, and you copy the data. Assign a class, and you copy the reference—both variables point to the same object.

scenes.question: What happens when you assign a struct?
scenes.right: The data is copied, making two independent values.
scenes.say: Interview trap: What happens when you assign a struct? It's not just a reference—you're copying the actual data.
